sharedFixtures.docs/storage-contracts.md: OrdersWriter.createAndCommit returns a receipt containing orderId and aggregateRevision only after committing one transaction in ordersDatabase that inserts the created order and its outbox record. HTTP maps the receipt to 201 Created. No inventory, payment or shipping work is promised by this operation. OutboxRelay publishes retained intent independently with acks=all. ProjectionConsumer later reads OrderCreated and commits a row with the same revision to projectionDatabase.orders_view; this consumer may be paused without stopping the writer or relay. ProjectionOrderReader queries that table. PrimaryOrderReader issues a new transaction against the same authoritative ordersDatabase primary used by the writer; this route has no cache, replica, or pre-existing transaction snapshot. Its read contract includes the previously committed creation. Notifications and analytics have independent subscriptions. The retained outbox, duplicate handling and relay recovery are established existing components outside this document review.
sharedFixtures.docs/checkout-flow.md:
# Checkout completion

POST /orders commits order creation and returns 201 with orderId and aggregateRevision. The UI then calls GET /orders/{id}; this read must include the newly created order. Waiting for a Kafka publication acknowledgement ensures that the query data is fresh. Requests have a 250 ms response budget and must not wait indefinitely. Pending notifications and analytics do not affect successful order creation.
